chapter: Sharkey, Chicago and the hot men
title: How Sharkey Bonano started: clarinet, trumpet and Johnny Carella
summary: Debate over whether Sharkey played clarinet first, how he got a trumpet, his age, and Johnny Carella's drugstore and restaurant.

blocks.x: He was playing clarinet at that time.

Sharky no. He told me he started playing clarinet. No, I never played no clarinet. Sharky no played no clarinet. No, he wanted to play clarinet. I gave him a card. And you better know what he said, of course I said, let him play a little boy.
I'll get paid, you know? Yeah.

That's what I care. Well, whose place was it that he took? Who? Johnny Carella finally hired him in the band. No. No, after that Johnny Carella died. He said that somebody, Johnny Stein or somebody like that was in the band and they went to Chicago and took somebody's place and that's how he got to be a trumpet player. Who?
Sharky. No, that came up around 19. When you were, when you were, when you were, when you were, when you were at the ringside?

Huh? That was late 1930 or so. That's when, that's when, that's when, Sharky went dead for him. Nobody worried about him, he could thank him for bringing him back. No, no man. No, no. Sharky had a little band.

No, he didn't play his brother. No, he died and everything before Sharky got to play good. When they broke up in Milenburg about 30 years ago, 35 years ago, they broke it down and everything.
